source.title: Five Architectures, One Shared Space Cross-Model Representational Alignment Without Weight Merging
source.authors: O. Anthonio; Dimeji AbdulSobur Olawuyi; O. Ajayi; T. Aderemi

record.file_problem: None apparent; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: It directly measures cross-model representational correspondence and tests mappings between representations, using distance-matrix agreement, nearest-neighbor matching, and retrieval through aligned spaces rather than reproducing the original study’s method. It does not test scaling.
record.gate_note: The paper reports cross-model similarity and aligned-space retrieval results, which bear on V4, V6, and V7. Pooling comparisons are used to choose a representation and report within-model category separation, not cross-model alignment, so they are not rows. The routing and task-accuracy results do not measure the claim’s representational behavior and are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study directly tests cross-model mapping, input-dependent alignment, and incomplete representational correspondence using five frozen language models. It does not test convergence with scale.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is substantially accurate. The authors report replicable final-layer correspondence and useful orthogonally aligned retrieval, weaker middle-layer correspondence, and limited transfer to symbolic inputs. Their strongest-layer statement excludes high embedding agreement attributed to lexical overlap. They find no routing benefit, do not test scaling, and do not identify the cause of shared structure.
record.recipe_differences: Measures pairwise cosine-distance agreement, nearest-neighbor matching, and held-out retrieval after linear mapping or generalized orthogonal Procrustes alignment. It compares five small language models at selected relative depths rather than testing alignment as models scale. No image-caption or cross-modal comparison.
record.method_sensitivity: Agreement varies with depth and model-pair group. Retrieval varies by input content and by whether code and multilingual probes are included in fitting. GPA and pairwise linear maps also differ by depth; GPA does better at the final layer, while pairwise maps do better in the middle layers. Embedding-layer agreement is attributed to lexical overlap.
record.problems: The study tests only five 1–2B-parameter base models and does not test scaling, instruction-tuned models, or capability-linked alignment. Probe sets were authored by the researchers. Retrieval pools are small (10 or 32 items). The shared dimension plateau is limited by training-fold rank. There was one run per checkpoint; no seed sweep was conducted. Mean pooling may understate Mamba. The authors also note that the tested content types are few and that some task analyses are low-powered.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant results were left out. The paper’s pooling ablation reports within-model separation and was used to select pooling, not to measure cross-model alignment. Stage 4 routing and task-accuracy results do not measure representational convergence.

untested.parts: No size or capability sweep tests increasing convergence.
No vision models or paired image-caption representations.
No same-architecture comparison across training initializations.

No functional layer substitution, stitching, relative representations, unpaired alignment, or preservation of downstream task performance through mapped representations. Retrieval uses small candidate pools.
No identification or comparison of interpretable features or circuits.
No controlled similarity-metric or neighbor-count sweep, and no cross-model pooling comparison. Alignment-method comparisons do not establish similarity-metric dependence.
No scale-dependent plateau or controlled test of shared training data or objectives as causes. The dimension plateau is explicitly sample-rank limited.

missing.what: Cross-model agreement in final-layer category-geometry changes: the three reorganizing transformers correlate 0.33–0.77, whereas Mamba's changes correlate −0.36 to 0.34 with other models. This adds evidence of heterogeneous correspondence.

The transformer–Mamba nearest-neighbor gap is only 0.014 and 0.004 at 75% depth, compared with approximately 0.16 and 0.17 at the final layer. Final-layer group means alone omit this depth interaction.

Probe-level distance correlations with length or lexical-rarity distances are at most 0.10 for four models and 0.18 for OLMo. These controls constrain shallow explanations of the incomplete agreement but do not identify its cause.

record.verdict_notes: V6 is itself a dependence claim, so demonstrated dependence supports it. V7 states incompleteness, so incomplete agreement is an observed instance of that version. Retrieval failure after a restricted, sample-fitted map is insufficient by itself to establish intrinsic representational incompleteness. No source access beyond the supplied text was used.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep over model size or capability, and no test of whether alignment rises as models get larger or more capable.
No vision models, paired images and captions, or test of alignment increasing with vision- or language-model performance.
No comparison of same-architecture models trained from different initializations, shared features, or shared subspaces across seeds.

Tests activation-based linear maps and orthogonal GPA alignment for five language models; does not test layer stitching, relative representations, unpaired alignment, or feature-level interchangeability.
No interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits are compared across models.

Tests depth and input-content dependence and reports results for multiple similarity/retrieval measures. It does not establish cross-model similarity under alternative pooling schemes; the pooling ablation is not a cross-model alignment test.

Finds incomplete or weaker alignment in some depths, model pairs, and input types. It does not test whether shared training data or objectives, rather than a common model of reality, cause the alignment.
